floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 9 re-confirmed (verdict C, 91/90 insns); gap mapped to 2 axes (1 combine-fold BF68[0] + 8-op sched1 reorder); fresh finding: D_8009BF68 externs disagree (array vs fn-ptr).

frontier.hypothesis: H-B1: a C statement-order / liveness lever flips the sched1 fmt-vs-BF78 load-order tie-break (8 of 9 ops).
frontier.mechanism: sched.c insn priority / LUID tie-break in the first debug_printf arg setup; loading fmt before the BF78 chain steers the early *stat_reg read into $v0.
frontier.next_probe: run tmp/gccdbg/cc1 (WSL) with BB2_SCHED_DEBUG=1 BB2_PRIO_DEBUG=1 on the sandbox .i; read priority values for fmt-LUI vs BF78-LUI; derive the C lever. Prior block-scoped/fmt-local/(void)-read nudges did NOT move the schedule.

frontier.hypothesis: H-A2: declaring/accessing D_8009BF68 consistent with its true scalar function-pointer type (not int array) emits the materialized non-folded load target wants (1 op).
frontier.mechanism: a scalar (non-array) symbol read vs array[0] read can present a different address RTL to combine.c; only the fn-ptr CAST was tried, not a consistent scalar fn-ptr declaration+read.
frontier.next_probe: probe scalar fn-ptr read shape now; and adopt sibling func_8007D3F8's committed BF68 decl once it matches (queue ~43, only other user).

frontier.hypothesis: H-A1: a combine.c-informed declaration shape suppresses the offset-0 symbol+0 fold in pure C (1 op).
frontier.mechanism: combine.c folds (mem (plus symbol_ref 0)) -> (mem symbol_ref); defeat-combine-symbol-fold excludes offset 0.
frontier.next_probe: read tools/gcc-2.7.2/combine.c symbol+0 simplification path for a fold-suppressing decl/access shape reachable from C; avoid the already-killed fold-defeat family.
